Setup
To setup your device, select the guide that corresponds to your operating system.
Your First Assignment
When working on assignments, ensure that your terminal's working directory is correct (which is likely where you unzipped the assignment).
1) What Would Python Do? (WWPD)

One component of lab assignments is to predict how the Python interpreter will
behave. We call these questions "What Would Python Do?"

In this class, we use a program called ok to assess your knowledge.
ok will be included with every assignment. Let's go through
how to do a WWPD question with ok.

Open your terminal, and make sure you are in the lab00 directory that contains
the unzipped lab files for this assignment. In that directory, type ls to verify
that there are the following files:
lab00.py: the starter file for this lab
ok: our testing program
lab00.ok: a configuration file for ok
If you don't see these files, use cd to navigate to the correct directory.
Attempting to run ok in a directory that does not have ok will produce an error.
Enter the following in your terminal, which will run ok and begin this section:

The command python3 ok -q python-basics -u tells the Python interpreter
to run the file with the name ok in the current working directory.
-q python-basics -u are inputs provided to the ok program that identify
which question to run.

As stated in the setup section, if the python3 command does not work,
please try using python or py.

You will be prompted to enter the output of various statements/expressions.
You must enter them correctly to move on, but there is no penalty for
incorrect answers.

The first time you run Ok, you will be prompted for your bCourses email.
Please follow {0}.
2) Implementing Functions

Open the entire lab00 folder in VS Code. You can drag the folder onto the VS
Code application or open VS Code and use Open Folder... in the File menu.
Once you open the lab00 folder, you'll see the lab00.py file in the file
explorer on the left panel of your VS Code window. Click it to start editing
lab00.py, which is the file you will submit to receive credit for the lab.

Important: Turn on Auto Save in the File menu of VS Code. Then, whenever
you change a file, the contents will be saved. If you don't enable Auto Save,
be sure to frequently save your work.

Recommended: Use the terminal inside VS Code (Terminal > New Terminal in
the menu). If you opened the assignment folder in VS Code as instructed above,
then the VS Code terminal's working directory will automatically be set to the
assignment folder, which means you won't have to change directories to check
your work.

Now complete the lab. You should see a function called twenty_twenty_six that
has a blank return statement. That blank is the only part you should change.
Replace it with an expression that evaluates to 2026.  What's the most creative
expression you can come up with?

Lab 1 Solutions
What does the modulo operator (%) do?
It calculates the remainder of a division.
What is the difference between return and print?
Return terminates a function call immediately, while print does not.
Print displays text without quotes, while return displays text with quotes.
What is the difference between true division (/) and floor division (//)?
Floor division truncates the result of true division.
Lab 2 Solutions
What is a higher order function?
A function that takes in another function as input, returns a function as output, or both.
What is the parent frame of a function?
Frame in which the function was defined (not called).
Why do we use higher order functions?
DRY (don't repeat yourself), generalization
We must create a function to take x using lambda or def, then compare the two quantities.

One question that might be nice to ask is:
in what ways is the logic for count_fives and count_primes similar,
and in what ways are they different?

The answer to the first question can tell us the logic that we want to
include in our count_cond function, while the answer to the second
question can tell us where in count_cond we want to be able to have
the difference in behavior observed between count_fives and
count_primes.

It'll be helpful to also keep in mind that we want count_cond to return
a function that, when an argument n is passed in, will behave similarly
to count_fives or count_primes. In other words, count_cond is a
higher order function that returns a function, that then contains the
logic common to both count_fives and count_primes.
Lab 3 Solutions
Why is type checking good practice and how can you use it to help you solve problems?
It helps catches bugs while you write your code and it helps you think about the inputs and solve problems!
Is there any scenario we would use list comprehension over regular lists?
It's more concise and in recursive functions it can build the result in the same line, especially useful for tree recursion for nested list construction.
How do you index the first, the middle, and last element of a list?

Given a list lst, index the first element using lst[0], middle with lst[len(lst) // 2], and last with lst[-1].
  (Technically this way of accessing the middle element will give the right middle element in even lists)
Lab 4 Solutions
What are the two restrictions for a key in a dictionary?
A key must be unique and a key cannot be a list or a dictionary
Why is it important not to violate the abstraction barrier?
They separate parts of a program so that changes in one part won't affect another
Describe the tree's constructor function
tree(label, branches=[]) returns a tree object with a root node called label and the specified branches
Lab 5 Solutions
What is the difference between the "is" operator and the "==" operator?
"is" checks if expressions on both sides evaluate to the same object, while "==" checks if they evaluate to equal values.
What does the map function do?
map takes a function and an iterable as arguments and returns a new iterator over the function applied to each element of the original iterable.
Does calling a generator function execute its body? Why or why not?
Calling a generator function does not execute its body. Instead, it returns a generator, which, when iterated through, executes the body.
Lab 6 Solutions
What is the main goal of Object Oriented Programming?

Classes create abstraction barriers between the use and implementation of data. A class serves as a template for all objects whose type is that class, and you can create multiple objects that store different data.
What is the difference between an instance variable and a class variable?
An instance variable is specific to a given object and different between objects, whereas a class variable is something that belongs to the class as a whole.
Do we have to explicitly pass in “self” when calling a method?
No, when one of an object's methods is called, the object is implicitly provided as the argument for self.

Remember that next must return a VirFib object! With this in mind, our
first goal is to calculate the next VirFib object and return it. One
approach is to figure out the base case (self.value == 0) and then decide what
information is needed for the following call to next.

You might also note that storing the current value makes the solution look very
similar to the iterative version of the virfib problem.
Lab 7 Solutions
What's the difference between the mutable tree class and the tree constructor and selector functions you've seen before?
Implemented as a class, can mutate the tree versus having to return a new tree every time
How do we get the label, branches, and figure out if a tree is a leaf?
tree.label, tree.branches, tree.is_leaf()
Lab 8 Solutions
For all of the questions, let link be the instance. They should know this distinction.
How do you check if the next element in a Linked List is empty?
Check if link.rest is Link.empty
How do you retrieve the element 3 from Link(2, Link(3))?
You use link.rest.first. It's important to realize that .rest still returns a Link OR Link.empty.
Why should you use Link.empty instead of an empty tuple () or null/falsy values

Breaks the abstraction barrier and there's more risk for error (is can help check reliably because Link.empty
  is a class attribute)!
Lab 9 Solutions
What parts of Scheme are similar to what we learned in Python?
It is a functional programming language that is recursive-based, lexical scoped, and all lists are linked lists!
What are the different ways you can create a list in scheme?

cons chains, list procedures, quote ' ` for creation; append, map, reduce, and filter are useful
  for list transformation/derivations.
What are some resources you can refer to if you ever need help on Scheme?
Refer to the Scheme Specification/Built-Ins under the Resources tab!
Lab 10 Solutions
What are the three steps of evaluation for a Scheme expression?
First evaluate the operand (check that it exists in the current frame), then evaluate the operands, and finally apply the operator to the operands.
What is the purpose of macros?
Macros in Scheme let you create your own commands by changing code before it runs.
Why is tail recursion beneficial in Scheme?
Tail recursion is beneficial because it allows frames that won't be used in the future to be closed, which saves space.
Lab 11 Solutions
What order do the clauses in a SQL command appear in?
When would you use where versus having?
Having is used after group by on aggregated rows, where is used when group by not applied yet.
How do you give a table an alias in a SQL command?
table AS alias

Ants Vs. SomeBees
The bees are coming!
Create a better soldier
With inherit-ants.
For full credit:
Submit with Phase 1 and Phase 2 complete by Thursday 07/23.
Submit with all phases complete by Tuesday 07/28.

Solve the problems in order, since some later problems depend on earlier
problems.

You can get 1 bonus point by submitting the entire project by
Monday 07/27.

In this project, you will create a {0} game called Ants Vs.
SomeBees. You populate your colony with the bravest ants you
can muster. Your ants must protect their queen from the evil bees invading
your territory. Irritate the bees enough by throwing leaves at them, and they
will be vanquished. Fail to pester the airborne intruders adequately, and your
queen will succumb to the bees' wrath. This game is inspired by PopCap Games'
{1}.

This project uses an object-oriented programming paradigm,
focusing on material from {0} of Composing Programs. The
project also involves understanding, extending, and testing a large program.

The {0} archive contains several files, but all of your
changes will be made to ants.py.
ants.py: The game logic of Ants Vs. SomeBees
ants_plans.py: The details of each difficulty level
ucb.py: Utility functions
gui.py: A graphical user interface (GUI) for Ants Vs. SomeBees.
ok: The autograder
proj3.ok: The ok configuration file
libs: A directory of libraries used by gui.py
static: A directory of images and files used by gui.py
